title: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer – Associate

domains.name: Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
ML Solution Monitoring, Maintenance, and Security

questions.question: A company stores a 20 TB tabular training dataset in S3. Training jobs only read a subset of columns. Which format minimizes storage and scan cost?
questions.explanation: Parquet is columnar and compressed, so engines can read only required columns. CSV and JSON require broader parsing; RecordIO is record-oriented.

questions.question: A data scientist needs one centralized set of customer features for both batch training and low-latency inference. Which SageMaker capability is best?
questions.explanation: Feature Store provides an offline store for training/batch workflows and an online store for low-latency feature retrieval, reducing training-serving skew.

questions.question: A stream requires multiple consumers, ordered records per shard, and replay capability. Which service should be selected?
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams retains records for replay and supports multiple consumers. Firehose is managed delivery rather than a replayable consumer stream.

questions.question: A processing job must join large S3 datasets from several systems and run custom distributed transformations. Which service is appropriate?
options: AWS Glue or Amazon EMR with Spark
questions.explanation: Glue provides managed serverless Spark ETL; EMR provides more Spark cluster control. Both support distributed joins and transformations.

questions.question: Training instances need concurrent shared POSIX access to a file system. Which storage option fits?
questions.explanation: EFS is an elastic shared POSIX file system. EBS is block storage attached to an instance; S3 is object storage.

questions.question: An image-classification project has unlabeled images and needs a managed human-labeling workflow. Which service should be used?
questions.explanation: SageMaker Ground Truth creates labeled datasets with human workers and active learning. Clarify analyzes bias/explanations after data/model preparation.

questions.question: A numeric feature has extreme positive values and a heavily right-skewed distribution. Which transformation commonly reduces this skew?
questions.explanation: A log transformation compresses large positive values and often makes long-tailed distributions easier to model. Encoding techniques are for categorical/text data.

questions.question: A nominal column has values red, green, and blue, with no meaningful ordering. Which encoding is normally appropriate?
questions.explanation: One-hot encoding avoids introducing a false ordinal relationship. Label encoding is safer for ordinal categories or some tree-based workflows with careful handling.

questions.question: A classifier reports 98% accuracy but almost never detects the rare fraud class. What data issue should be investigated first?
questions.explanation: Class imbalance can make accuracy misleading. Evaluate recall, precision, and F1 for the rare class and consider resampling, class weights, or synthetic data.

questions.question: Which SageMaker service analyzes pre-training bias metrics and can explain model predictions?
questions.explanation: SageMaker Clarify supports pre-training bias, post-training bias, and feature attribution/explainability. Neo compiles models for edge targets.

questions.question: A team calculates normalization parameters using the full dataset before splitting it into train and test sets. What is the primary risk?
questions.explanation: Using test-set information while fitting preprocessing leaks future evaluation information into training. Fit preprocessing on the training set only, then apply it to validation/test data.

questions.question: A model processes historical events where later records must not influence earlier predictions. Which split strategy is correct?
questions.explanation: A time-aware split preserves chronology and prevents future information from leaking into training. Random splits can leak future patterns for temporal data.

questions.question: A training job cannot read SSE-KMS encrypted S3 input despite having s3:GetObject. What permission is commonly missing?
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS access requires both S3 access and KMS key permission such as kms:Decrypt through IAM/key policy.

questions.question: A team needs visual no-code profiling, cleaning, and transformation of tabular data. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Glue DataBrew provides visual no-code data preparation. Data Wrangler is ML-focused and also valid for SageMaker workflows, but DataBrew directly fits this requirement.

questions.question: A company needs managed translation between languages and does not need custom model training. What is the best service?
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate is the managed AI service for language translation. Training a custom model adds unnecessary operational work for this standard use case.

questions.question: A binary classifier must minimize false negatives because missed disease cases are costly. Which metric should receive high priority?
questions.explanation: Recall measures the fraction of actual positives that are detected. High recall reduces false negatives; precision focuses on false positives.

questions.question: A model has excellent training metrics but substantially worse validation metrics. What is the likely problem?
questions.explanation: A large train-validation gap is a classic overfitting signal. Consider regularization, more data, augmentation, early stopping, or a simpler model.

questions.question: A team needs to search hyperparameters efficiently based on results from previous trials. Which method best fits?
questions.explanation: Bayesian optimization uses prior trial outcomes to select promising configurations, often reducing expensive training trials. SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning supports managed tuning workflows.

questions.question: What is the purpose of early stopping during training?
options: Stop when validation performance no longer improves
questions.explanation: Early stopping halts training when the monitored validation metric stops improving, saving cost and helping limit overfitting.

questions.question: A team uses custom PyTorch code for training. Which SageMaker capability supports this most directly?
questions.explanation: SageMaker script mode supports custom training scripts with supported frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow.

questions.question: A company needs a traceable model approval process with versions, metadata, and promotion states. Which service should be used?
questions.explanation: Model Registry tracks model package versions, metadata, approval status, and supports governed promotion into deployment workflows.

questions.question: A regression model must penalize large prediction errors more than small errors. Which metric is appropriate?
questions.explanation: RMSE squares errors before aggregation, so large errors have greater impact. Recall/F1/ROC-AUC are classification metrics.

questions.question: A team needs a managed foundation model for text summarization without hosting model infrastructure. Which service is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock provides managed access to foundation models for inference and customization. It avoids hosting the model infrastructure directly.

questions.question: A model performs poorly on both training and validation datasets. What condition is most likely?
questions.explanation: Poor training and validation performance suggests underfitting. Consider higher model capacity, better features, more training, or less regularization.

questions.question: Which technique randomly disables neural-network units during training to reduce co-adaptation?
questions.explanation: Dropout is a regularization technique that randomly disables units during training to improve generalization.

questions.question: A candidate model should receive production-like requests without affecting customer responses. Which strategy should be used?
questions.explanation: Shadow testing sends production-like traffic to a candidate model while the production model remains customer-facing. It enables safe comparison.

questions.question: A team needs to identify exploding gradients and tensor-level training issues. Which SageMaker capability helps?
questions.explanation: SageMaker Debugger captures and analyzes training tensors and rules to help diagnose convergence issues such as exploding or vanishing gradients.

questions.question: A workload scores millions of S3 records every night and does not require interactive responses. Which inference option is best?
questions.explanation: Batch Transform processes datasets in bulk without keeping a persistent endpoint running, which fits scheduled offline scoring.

questions.question: An inference request contains a large payload and processing can take several minutes. Which SageMaker deployment type fits?
questions.explanation: Asynchronous inference queues long-running or large-payload requests and writes output to S3. Real-time endpoints are designed for lower-latency synchronous calls.

questions.question: An application has infrequent unpredictable traffic and wants no instance management for a small model. Which option is suitable?
questions.explanation: Serverless inference automatically scales for intermittent traffic without managing instances. Consider startup and model/runtime constraints.

questions.question: A new model must receive 10% of traffic first and be rolled back if errors or latency rise. Which approach is best?
questions.explanation: A canary deployment routes a small percentage of traffic to the new variant and supports measured promotion or rollback.

questions.question: A team needs repeatable SageMaker endpoints, roles, alarms, and VPC resources across environments. Which practice is best?
options: Infrastructure as code with CloudFormation or CDK
questions.explanation: CloudFormation or CDK version the infrastructure and make environments repeatable. Manual console setup is difficult to audit and reproduce.

questions.question: A real-time endpoint must increase capacity as requests per instance rise. Which capability should be configured?
questions.explanation: Endpoint autoscaling can use metrics such as InvocationsPerInstance, latency, or CPU utilization to adjust capacity.

questions.question: A SageMaker endpoint needs private access to an internal database. What configuration is required?
options: Place the endpoint in VPC subnets with appropriate security groups
questions.explanation: VPC configuration with suitable subnets, routes, and security groups enables private connectivity to internal resources.

questions.question: A workflow must run preprocessing, training, evaluation, conditional registration, and deployment as an ML-native DAG. Which service is best?
questions.explanation: SageMaker Pipelines natively orchestrates ML workflow steps, including condition-based model registration and deployment decisions.

questions.question: A CI pipeline must run unit tests and build a container image before model deployment. Which service runs these build steps?
questions.explanation: CodeBuild runs tests and builds artifacts/images. CodePipeline orchestrates stages; CodeDeploy handles supported deployment actions.

questions.question: A retraining pipeline should run monthly and also when a drift alert occurs. Which service can trigger both schedules and event-based workflows?
questions.explanation: EventBridge supports scheduled rules and event routing. It can trigger SageMaker Pipelines or Step Functions for retraining workflows.

questions.question: A model team has hundreds of models using the same container and only a few are invoked at any time. Which endpoint pattern can reduce endpoint sprawl?
questions.explanation: Multi-model endpoints dynamically load models from S3 into a shared endpoint/container, suitable for many similar infrequently used models.

questions.question: Production input feature distributions now differ from the training baseline. What condition is this?
questions.explanation: Data drift is a change in production input data distribution compared with the training/baseline data. It can affect model quality.

questions.question: Which SageMaker capability monitors production data quality and model-quality constraint violations?
questions.explanation: Model Monitor detects data quality, model quality, bias drift, and feature attribution drift issues against configured baselines.

questions.question: A team needs request latency, endpoint errors, and custom operational alarms. Which service is central to this?
questions.explanation: CloudWatch provides metrics, logs, dashboards, and alarms for endpoint/infrastructure monitoring and operational response.

questions.question: A model endpoint is expensive because it remains running overnight with no traffic. What is the most direct first action?
options: Stop/delete unused endpoint or use a suitable on-demand pattern
questions.explanation: Persistent real-time endpoints accrue cost while provisioned. Remove unused endpoints or select serverless, asynchronous, or batch inference when requirements permit.

questions.question: Which tool analyzes historical AWS spending by service, tag, and time period?
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer analyzes and forecasts costs by dimensions such as service, account, tag, and period. Budgets adds threshold alerts.

questions.question: An organization needs an alert before ML project spending exceeds a monthly target. Which service should it use?
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets sets cost or usage thresholds and sends alerts. Cost Explorer analyzes costs but does not provide the primary budget-alert workflow.

questions.question: A user can access an encrypted S3 bucket but a SageMaker training job fails to read objects. Which two permissions should be considered?
options: S3 data access and KMS decrypt permission
questions.explanation: For SSE-KMS objects, the training role needs S3 access and permission to use the KMS key, including kms:Decrypt where appropriate.

questions.question: Which identity pattern is best for a SageMaker training job accessing AWS resources?
options: An IAM execution role with least privilege
questions.explanation: Use a least-privilege IAM execution role. Do not embed static credentials or use root credentials for workload access.

questions.question: A security team must know who changed a production endpoint configuration and when. Which service provides the audit trail?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail records API and management events, including identities, time, source IP, and actions related to endpoint changes.

questions.question: A model service calls several downstream services and needs end-to-end request tracing. Which AWS service helps?
questions.explanation: X-Ray traces requests through distributed applications and helps identify latency or failure points across service boundaries.

questions.question: An endpoint must reach private resources but must not be publicly exposed. Which design is appropriate?
options: Private VPC subnets and restrictive security groups
Public endpoint with open security group
questions.explanation: Private subnets and restrictive security groups isolate ML resources. Add only required routes/VPC endpoints and apply least-privilege IAM.

questions.question: A candidate model should only be promoted automatically if it meets a defined evaluation threshold. Where should this gate be implemented?
options: A conditional step in SageMaker Pipelines
questions.explanation: A SageMaker Pipelines condition step can evaluate a metric and register/promote only models that meet the defined threshold.
